messages:
Aisha: Heads-up, seeing a sustained spike of NVIDIA Xid 48 in us-east1 A10 pool starting ~02:10 UTC. ~180 events/min across 6 racks, skewed to tenants doing many tiny (1-4 token) RPCs.

Aisha: Quick grep from node logs (pulled from /var/log/messages):
```
Mar 20 02:10:12 gpu-node-07 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 48, PID=3245, CE: single-bit ECC error detected
Mar 20 02:10:12 gpu-node-07 kernel: pcieport 0000:5e:00.0: AER: Corrected error received: id=00e4
Mar 20 02:10:13 gpu-node-07 kernel: eth0: link down
Mar 20 02:10:13 gpu-node-07 kernel: eth0: link up
```

devon: looking now. initial correlates: small-batch/high-qps tenants share same top-of-rack NICs; I'm seeing repeated PCIe AER corrected errors concurrent with NIC flaps.

devon: dmesg snippet from affected host: 
```
[  123.456789] pcieport 0000:5e:00.0: AER: Uncorrected (Non-Fatal) error; device recovery required
[  123.456790] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 48, PID=5678, CE: single-bit ECC error detected
```

mike_ops: Did we recently change the small-batch routing/kernel? The tiny-allocation path we shipped last week moves lots of DMA descriptors per request. Could be churning DMA/PCIe resources.

katie: Canary for the small-batch rollout hit those racks 02:05–02:12 UTC, same time window. Canary QPS peaked at ~1200 r/s but in tiny token size shape.

noah: From ops perspective: these hosts are in Dedicated reserved pool, we can't pull full capacity offline. Need targeted card-level maintenance or live-migrate tenants.

devon: Proposed mitigation steps:
1) soft-drain affected cards on 4 hosts (mark GPUs unschedulable, allow in-flight jobs to finish)
2) route affected tenants to adjacent racks using routing policy override (traffic-shift, 5–10% per minute)
3) capture NVML logs and ECC counters before replacement, enable kdump on one repro node
4) file hardware RMA for suspicious cards (4 candidates) and schedule firmware bump after swap

jira-bot: Created ticket INF-5249: "us-east1 A10 Xid48 spike - sparse-concurrency netlink" assigned to eng-infra.

Aisha: +1 on that plan. Cost/contract note: moving tenants within Dedicated pool will temporarily increase cross-rack egress; finance informed but impact should be small for <24h.

noah: Replacement ETA: parts + tech slot ~48h, but we can start soft-drains and RMA initiation now.

devon: Observability checklist I'm collecting (will attach to INF-5249):
- prometheus query for ECC single-bit rate: `sum(rate(nv_gpu_ecc_errors_corrected_total[5m])) by (gpu)`
- nvml pmon dumps for top offenders
- kernel AER logs and pci-states pre/post drain

mike_ops: Hypothesis: older A10 firmware + repeated small DMA bursts -> NIC link retries -> AER triggers Xid48 on single-bit ECC counters. If true, firmware bump + card swap should reduce recurrence.

Aisha: Next steps: devon start drains on `gpu-node-07, gpu-node-12, gpu-node-23, gpu-node-31` in that order. katie coordinate traffic-shift. noah start RMA. I'll draft customer advisory for affected tenants (opt-out to CPU fallback for short window). :thumbsup:

Aisha: I'll update thread when drains complete or if we see new error classes (13/31) pop up. Thanks all.
